David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Cerebras Systems reported better-than-expected results and quarterly guidance in its earnings report on Thursday, and touted a new deal with Microsoft . The stock climbed about 7% on Friday. Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus: Earnings per share: 12 cents adjusted vs. loss of 14 cents expected Core revenue: $230.9 million vs. $214.7 million expected Cerebras' core revenue grew 70% from $135.7 million, compared with 103% growth in the second quarter, according to a statement . "I think there is opportunity created by, particularly on the hardware side, the sale of hardware, where long lead times in GPUs and more expense creates opportunity for us," Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman told CNBC in an interview, referring to graphics processing units. Executives will announce a new relationship with Microsoft , one of the world's top cloud providers, on a conference call with analysts, Feldman said. The call starts at 5 p.m. ET. "We believe revenue begins to show up in Q1 '27," Feldman said in the interview, adding that Microsoft signed the deal in October. Cerebras has also landed deals with other major cloud providers Amazon and Oracle . The company is trying to challenge Nvidia in the AI chip market. Its earnings land on the same day that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company he co-founded after multiple scandals involving extramarital affairs. For the fourth quarter, Cerebras expects a core gross margin of 47% to 49%, with $310 million to $330 million in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for a 42.1% margin and $271 million in revenue. Cerebras said it expects revenue to triple in 2027. That implies about $2.85 billion in revenue.
